observable_before: Bare Go creates a syntactic intent task without grounded repository exploration.
Repeated rough intake can create suffixed duplicate tasks.
Advice/planning provenance does not itself gate a materialized task claim.
observable_after: A bounded read-only adapter assesses a versioned repository snapshot and returns explicit reuse, update or create actions.
Applying the same assessment is idempotent and preserves every original outcome/source plus later feedback.
Planning/advice authority and unresolved user questions block only affected task claims; independent authorized work remains eligible.
An unknown bug root cause can materialize research, never a claimed implementation fix.
states_and_edges: planning/advice -> explicit execute promotion before claim
unresolved question -> affected task blocked while independent task remains claimable
unknown bug -> research task -> later implementation dependency
non_goals: No keyword or schema heuristic presented as semantic quality.
No automatic vision or decision-ledger rewrite.
No task execution or publication during intake.
No new agent/provider protocol; reuse the released adapter boundary.
dependencies: go_workflow adapter protocol and controlled model selection
existing R# outcome, architecture and dependency claim gates
delegated_choices: Exact JSON field names and CLI spelling are reversible implementation choices within the task scope.
The assessment can use the existing critic/read-only adapter phase because this is evaluation, not product mutation.
proof: Adapter-double tests prove exact request transport and persisted result binding without claiming model intelligence.
Positive/negative tests cover reuse, repeated apply, feedback preservation, superseded decisions, unknown bugs, questions and authority gates.
A real bounded Codex assessment is retained as run evidence before release.
Declared focused tests, make check, content-bound completion, critic and immutable release/readback close R1-R5.
